summary: Many massive data centers use BGP as their single routing protocol. This RFC describes BGP Link State extensions that apply Shortest Path First routing, so BGP can work like a link-state protocol while staying simple to operate.

eli5.summary: BGP usually passes along only the best directions. This lets it share a whole map so each router can compute shortest routes.

bgp as link state routing in data centers
subtitle: How BGP can act like a link-state protocol, so every router builds a full map and runs Dijkstra's shortest path first algorithm.

tldr.problem: Many massively scaled data centers use BGP as their only routing protocol, but ordinary BGP path-vector routing gives each router only a view of the best paths, and one link failure can touch hundreds or thousands of prefixes.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9815 defines a new BGP-LS-SPF address family (SAFI 80) that carries BGP-LS node, link and prefix information. Each router floods it right away, keeps the latest version, and runs the Shortest Path First (Dijkstra) algorithm on the map in place of the normal BGP decision process.
tldr.outcome: BGP speakers get a complete topology view, fast propagation of changes and support for ECMP and fast reroute, while keeping BGP as the single protocol. It is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted.

today: RFC 9815 is a Proposed Standard published in July 2025, and no later RFC obsoletes or updates it. Deployment guidance for the peering models is in the companion RFC 9816.

sections.title: Why Run SPF Over BGP
sections.content:
Many Massively Scaled Data Centers (MSDCs) have converged on simplified Layer 3 routing, and for operational simplicity many use BGP as their single routing protocol for both fabric routing and Data Center Interconnect (DCI) routing. RFC 7938 already describes that approach. RFC 9815 offers an alternative that borrows the BGP Link State (BGP-LS) encodings from RFC 9552 and the Shortest Path First (SPF) algorithm used by Interior Gateway Protocols (IGPs).

The RFC lists the advantages it is after: TCP-based flow control, no periodic link-state refresh, and completely incremental NLRI advertisement. Every BGP speaker in the domain has a complete view of the topology, which supports ECMP and IP fast reroute (such as Loop-Free Alternatives) without advertising extra BGP paths.

The saving on failures is the main point. With standard BGP path-vector routing, a single link failure may impact hundreds or thousands of prefixes. With BGP SPF, only the speakers originating the Link NLRI need to withdraw it, and a changed NLRI is advertised immediately instead of only after best-route selection.
sections.eli5: Imagine one road closes. Old BGP is like telling every town about every route that used that road. With a shared map, you only say "this road is closed" and everyone updates their own plans.

sections.title: How It Relates to BGP and BGP-LS
sections.content:
Apart from the Decision Process, BGP SPF uses the BGP protocol of RFC 4271 unchanged: the finite state machine, messages and their encodings, attributes, NLRI encodings and error handling all stay. The Decision Process is changed in three ways. Advertisements are passed on immediately without waiting for route computation. The phase 1 preference step is replaced by the NLRI selection rules. Phase 2 is replaced by the SPF algorithm, also called the Dijkstra algorithm.

BGP-LS in RFC 9552 already defines NLRIs for nodes, links and prefixes. Rather than reuse the BGP-LS SAFI, the RFC introduces the BGP-LS-SPF SAFI so the existing BGP-LS usage stays backward compatible. The two SAFIs share the same TLV registry, and by default other BGP-LS TLVs are ignored for the new SAFI.

The SAFI value is 80, used with the BGP-LS AFI 16388. Two speakers MUST exchange the Multiprotocol Extensions Capability for AFI 16388 / SAFI 80 before they can exchange this NLRI. The modifications only apply to IPv4 and IPv6 as underlay unicast SAFIs.
sections.eli5: The new system keeps almost all of BGP's normal rules. Only the part where a router decides which route is best gets swapped for a map-and-shortest-path method, and it gets its own separate mailbox so older BGP-LS users are not confused.

sections.title: Peering Models
sections.content:
All speakers in a BGP SPF routing domain must follow this specification, but the choice of how they peer is up to the operator (deployment guidance is in RFC 9816). Three models are described.

  • Single-hop peering: External BGP sessions run over each direct point-to-point link. Once the session is up and the BGP-LS-SPF capability is exchanged, the link is up and its Link NLRI is advertised. If the session drops, the Link NLRIs are withdrawn.
  • Peering between directly connected nodes: sessions may run between loopback addresses, and liveness detection is independent of BGP. BFD is RECOMMENDED. There is one session even with several parallel links, so this model is RECOMMENDED over single-hop peering.
  • Route-reflector or controller peering: speakers peer only with route reflectors or controllers. This "sparse peering" needs fewer sessions and fewer copies of the same NLRI.

An End-of-RIB marker MAY be required from a peer before a Link NLRI is advertised to it. When required, the default is to wait indefinitely, and the RFC warns that inconsistent configuration can cause transient micro-loops and dropped traffic.
sections.eli5: Routers can talk to every neighbor on every wire, to each neighbor once, or just to a few helper routers who pass the news on. Fewer conversations means less to keep track of.

sections.title: NLRI and TLVs
sections.content:
The BGP-LS NLRI types carry the map. Node NLRI MUST be advertised unconditionally by all routers. Link NLRI describes a link between two nodes, and Prefix NLRI describes reachable IPv4 or IPv6 prefixes. Descriptors MUST include the BGP Router-ID and the Autonomous System number, and Node and Link NLRI MUST use the direct protocol (Protocol-ID 4).

Three TLVs matter most:

  • Sequence Number TLV (type 1181): mandatory, 8 octets, strictly increasing for every self-originated version of an NLRI, and it has to survive restarts. If it is missing, the NLRI is malformed.
  • SPF Status TLV (type 1184): shared by Node, Link and Prefix NLRI, one octet. It marks a node unreachable (1) or not supporting transit (2), a link unreachable (1), or a prefix unreachable (1). Values 0 and 255 are reserved and make the TLV malformed.
  • Address Family Link Descriptor TLV (type 1185): says whether an unnumbered link is used for IPv4 (1), IPv6 (2) or both.

The IGP Metric (TLV 1095) MUST be present on Link NLRI, and the Prefix Metric (TLV 1155) on Prefix NLRI, or they are not used. The metric length is 4 octets. A Link NLRI missing its metric is malformed. The BGP-LS Attribute can be large, so supporting extended messages from RFC 8654 is RECOMMENDED, and a route that does not fit in an UPDATE MUST NOT be advertised.
sections.eli5: The map is made of small labeled cards: one for each router, each wire between them, and each address. A version number on every card lets everyone know which copy is the newest, and a status sticker can say "this one is broken".

sections.title: NLRI Selection and the SPF Calculation
sections.content:
Each NLRI is originated by exactly one speaker, so selecting among copies is simple. The rules are applied in order: NLRI self-originated by a directly connected peer is preferred (which repairs stale data after a cold start); an NLRI from a peer replaces the same NLRI from that peer; the highest Sequence Number wins; and the numerically larger BGP Identifier is preferred. A less recent NLRI is stale and is not advertised. Other BGP attributes such as ORIGIN, MULTI_EXIT_DISC and LOCAL_PREF are ignored, and AS_PATH is kept only for loop detection.

If a speaker receives a self-originated NLRI that differs from its own, it advances its sequence number to one greater than the received value and readvertises. After the first such event, later ones are delayed by BGP_LS_SPF_SELF_READVERTISEMENT_DELAY (default 5 seconds), since a misconfigured or rogue speaker is likely.

The calculation is rooted at the local router and uses the IGP Metric and Prefix Metric. In outline:

  1. Invalidate the Local-RIB and start with an empty candidate list (CAN-LIST).
  2. Put the computing router at cost 0.
  3. Take the lowest-cost node off the list, skipping nodes marked unreachable.
  4. Install its prefixes, adding the prefix metric to the node's cost.
  5. Examine its links. A link is used only if the remote node advertises a matching link back, which is the bidirectional connectivity check. Nodes are added or updated on the list by cost, and equal-cost next-hops are merged to give ECMP.
  6. When the list is empty, add, update and remove changed routes in the GLOBAL-RIB.

Any optimization MUST give the same set of routes. Weighted unequal-cost multipath is out of scope. The calculation can be scheduled with the back-off algorithm of RFC 8405.
sections.eli5: Everybody has the same map and starts from their own house. They keep visiting the nearest unvisited place, noting the total distance, until every place has the shortest route written down. A road only counts if both ends agree it exists.

sections.title: Failure Convergence and Error Handling
sections.content:
Normally the link would stay in use until the last copy of its Link NLRI is withdrawn. To avoid that delay, the originator SHOULD first advertise a newer version with the SPF Status TLV saying the link is down, and withdraw it later. The suggested default for the LinkStatusDownAdvertise timer is 2 seconds, and prefixes work the same way with PrefixStatusDownAdvertise, also 2 seconds. If the link or prefix comes back during that period, the originator MUST advertise a newer version without the status TLV. For node failure, stale NLRIs do not delay convergence because adjacent nodes advertise the link as down and the bidirectional check fails.

Malformed SPF Status or Address Family Link Descriptor TLVs make the NLRI malformed, and it is handled as 'treat-as-withdraw' under RFC 7606. An update with no BGP-LS Attribute SHOULD still be propagated but MUST NOT be used in the SPF calculation. If two speakers lose database synchronization, the session MUST be reset unless other resynchronization is used, with a NOTIFICATION carrying the error "Loss of LSDB Synchronization".
sections.eli5: When a road breaks, the nearest neighbor shouts "closed!" straight away, and only later removes the road from the map. If the road reopens quickly, they send a fresh note saying so.

sections.title: Security and Operations
sections.content:
The RFC says it does not change the underlying security issues of BGP, and the considerations of RFC 4271 and BGP-LS apply. The speakers are expected to be under a single administrative domain, so inter-domain BGP security such as origin validation and BGPsec is considered out of scope. One notable denial-of-service attack is including malformed attributes in a replicated update so receivers treat the NLRI as withdrawn. To reduce the risk of masquerading peers, the TCP Authentication Option (RFC 5925) is RECOMMENDED for BGP sessions. If a speaker sees its own NLRI originated by another speaker, it SHOULD log an error.

Management guidance includes configuring metrics consistently across the domain, a recommended metric of 0 for loopback prefixes, configuring Remote Link Identifiers when there are parallel unnumbered links, an SPF log for troubleshooting, and keeping BGP-LS-SPF sessions isolated from other address families, for example with separate BGP instances or sessions.
sections.eli5: Because everyone trusts the shared map, a liar could mess it up. So routers should check who they are talking to, and complain loudly if someone else starts writing cards that claim to be theirs.

sections.title: IANA Assignments
sections.content:
IANA assigned SAFI value 80 for BGP-LS-SPF from the First Come First Served range, and TLV code points 1181 (Sequence Number), 1184 (SPF Status) and 1185 (Address Family Link Descriptor). Earlier early allocations for SPF Capability (1180), IPv4 Link Prefix Length (1182) and IPv6 Link Prefix Length (1183) are no longer required and are deprecated.

Three new registries hold the SPF Status values for Node, Link and Prefix NLRI, and IANA assigned value 9 for Loss of LSDB Synchronization in the BGP Error (Notification) Codes registry.
sections.eli5: The rule makers gave the new pieces official numbers, like assigning house numbers to new buildings, so nobody else reuses them.

items.label: Sequence Number
items.desc: Mandatory 8-octet strictly increasing number on every NLRI.

items.label: SPF Status
items.desc: Marks a node, link or prefix unreachable, or a node as no-transit.

items.label: Address Family Link Descriptor
items.desc: Says whether an unnumbered link serves IPv4, IPv6 or both.

items.label: Reserved
items.desc: Receiving it makes the TLV malformed.

items.label: Node unreachable
items.desc: Node is unreachable with respect to BGP SPF.

items.label: No transit
items.desc: Node does not support transit with respect to BGP SPF.

items.label: Unassigned
items.desc: Unknown values are ignored in the SPF computation.

items.label: Reserved
items.desc: Receiving it makes the TLV malformed.
